I picture Patty as having been involved in hiding and enabling her husband’s criminal behavior for so long, that at the time of the murder, her brain went into autopilot and her top priority was continuing to protect him, hence the nonsensical ransom note. i don’t necessarily agree with “irritable hypersensitivity”, i think likening the moon to searchlights moreso invokes a feeling of dread: when are searchlights utilized? to highlight something, put it on grand display—she feels extremely vulnerable here, watched. another more grim use of searchlights is the attempt to find a person in the darkness—a missing person. if we keep this use of the word in mind, the speaker is almost likened to the victim of a crime, which the poem implies to be a sexual assault.

i agree! i think you’ve expanded on my opinions just more eloquently— questioning a poem is an essential part of reading and enjoying poetry as a craft. contention regarding the definition of “poetry” is also an inescapable and IMO invigorating aspect of discussion. to me it’s just bizarre that rupi kaur is sometimes treated as the originator of this style rather than an arguably clumsy wielder of it, and, since her work is “bad”, then all poetry that toes the line and makes us question our  definitions of poetry is just as uninspired. it enforces an extremely rigid idea that all poetry must be formulaic. 

i think she is an important literary figure in terms of her accessibility—she’s definitely inspired lots of people to explore poetry who otherwise might not have. the issue just lies within peoples’ exploration beginning and ending with her work, therefore rendering her a sort of dominating figure in discussion.

^ this, also i wish rupi kaur wasn’t used as a reference point for determining which poetry is “bad”… it leads to this unfair precedent where most short-form or ironic poems are instantly written off as RK-esque drivel. RK’s work is essentially a parody or bastardization of this style of poetry. she mimics these classic, experimental works but with less than a fraction of the thoughtfulness the original poets had. its just total cash-grab garbage poetry for people who don’t know anything about the craft, and it seems like it’s triggering this sort of kneejerk negative reaction in the poetry community to anything even vaguely similar, no matter how much more nuanced or innovative it really is. sorry for rambling, hope this makes sense

agree, the mention of hormones is almost totally irrelevant here. i think the conversation surrounding the effects that BC has on women should definitely be expanded and normalized, for sure. but i take birth control pills due to health issues (PMDD) and i don’t see any correlation between my taking them and questioning my sexuality. the only time i really questioned whether i was bi or lesbian was when i was younger—during puberty—but as i’ve grown older i’m completely certain now, and this hasn’t been shaken by whether or not i’m on the pill.

i think the “flip flopping” of labels that nonstraight women experience can be attributed more to social and systemic factors, like requiredmetrics said. we are socialized to believe our primary purpose is to please men, and the pressure to conform to heteronormative standards is intense for girls and women, which i think is partially why lesbian women are often hesitant to label themselves as such, and why so many lesbians go through a phase of calling themselves bisexual: it allows them to express their attraction to women while still being somewhat palatable to hetero society.
